recognition.title: Recognition of prior learning and credits
recognition.purpose: How experience becomes recognised credit: evidence, two assessors, indicative NQF levels and credits.

my-recognition.title: My recognition (RPL)
my-recognition.purpose: Ask for credit for what you already do, build the evidence pack and answer attestation requests.

my-rpl.title: RPL request
my-rpl.purpose: One request: the evidence pack, the decision by two assessors, the statement and the NQC-ready export.

my-credits.title: My learning credits
my-credits.purpose: Your credit ledger, indicative NQF levels and progress on 30-credit stacks.

rpl-queue.title: RPL assessment queue
rpl-queue.purpose: Recommend, confirm as a second assessor, and open requests for contractors.

rpl-review.title: Review an RPL request
rpl-review.purpose: Weigh the evidence pack and record a maker-checker decision.

admin-credit-tags.title: NQF and credit tags
admin-credit-tags.purpose: Tag courses, pathways and micro-credentials with an indicative NQF level and credits.

my-learning-balance.title: My learning balance
my-learning-balance.purpose: Your annual learning balance in credits and hours, the mid-career top-up, the outcome-gated catalogue and protected study time.

team-study-time.title: Team study time
team-study-time.purpose: Decide your team's protected study time and see their learning balances.

workforce-learning-balances.title: Learning balances
workforce-learning-balances.purpose: The grant rule, how balances are used across the organisation and the study-time requests.

my-external-certs.title: My external certificates
my-external-certs.purpose: Add certificates from universities, professional bodies and online courses; a verifier checks them and the crosswalk maps them to skills.

external-certs-queue.title: External certificate verification
external-certs-queue.purpose: Verify, reject or revoke external certificates; only reviewed crosswalk rows map to skills.

ui.notAuthTitle: Kafa'a is not a licensing or regulatory authority
ui.notAuthBody: Recognition here is an internal record prepared for review by assessors recognised by the National Qualifications Centre. It never changes a licence or a qualification record, and qualification entries only mirror the licensee's records as qualified or not qualified.
ui.indicative: Indicative until agreed with the NQC and the partner.

advice.full: The pack looks sufficient for full credit at level {level}.
advice.partial: The pack supports partial credit at level {level}; more evidence would be needed for the requested level.
advice.not_yet: Not enough evidence yet: add records that name the skill or a confirmed attestation.

why.zero: {item}: counts nothing yet (not confirmed or not qualified)
why.need: Score {score} against {need} needed for the requested level (2 + 2 x level)
why.deep: Levels 3-4 also need two kinds of evidence and a confirmed supervisor attestation

detail.intro: Build the evidence pack from your own records, ask a supervisor to attest, then submit. Two different assessors decide.
detail.notFound: Request not found or not visible to you
detail.packDesc: Records from your own history. Security-restricted records never enter a pack.
detail.packEmptyBody: Attach at least two items, one of them a record, before you submit.
detail.adviceNote: The assessors decide; this only explains the weights.
detail.counted: {n} items count toward the statement (attestations only once confirmed).
detail.creditsNote: {c} credits recognised (indicative until agreed with the NQC and the partner).

tl.behalf: Opened by an assessor on behalf of a contractor

decision.title: Decision
decision.twoPeople: Recommended by {a}, confirmed by {b}: two different people.
decision.exportNote: Initials only, roles not names, no regulator wording.

picker.title: Add evidence from your records
picker.desc: OJT practice your preceptor acknowledged, simulator debriefs, the qualification mirror and signed-off engagements.
picker.emptyBody: Ask a supervisor for an attestation and add records as they are logged.
picker.secNote: Security, safeguards and cyber records follow the security career path and are refused if attached.

attestDrawer.title: Ask a supervisor to attest
attestDrawer.body: They will see only this request's target and your note, and answer in their own words.

actions.title: Next step
actions.ready: The pack is ready to submit.
actions.notReady: {n} usable items: attach at least 2, one of them a record.
actions.submitBody: An assessor reviews the pack, then a second assessor confirms. You cannot change the pack after submitting.
actions.withdrawBody: The request is kept as withdrawn; you can open a new one later.

review.intro: Weigh the evidence, then record a recommendation; a second assessor confirms or returns it.
review.title: Decision (maker-checker)
review.desc: Two different assessors, neither of them the person. Confirmation writes validated evidence and the credit.
review.checkOkBody: The recommendation passes the same checks the server runs.
review.recommendBody: A second assessor must confirm before any credit is written.
review.confirmBody: Credit is written as validated evidence, skills are recomputed, the statement is stored and a ledger entry is made.
review.returnBody: The recommendation is cleared and the request goes back to the first step of the review.

msg.forbidden: Staff open their own RPL requests; assessors open requests on behalf of contractors
msg.person: Choose an active member of staff or contractor
msg.behalf: Assessors open requests on behalf of contractors only; staff open their own
msg.target: Choose a skill or a micro-credential
msg.restricted: Security and cyber-hygiene skills are not recognised individually: they follow the security career path
msg.level: Choose a level from 1 to 4 where the skill exists
msg.held: You already hold this at that level: nothing to recognise
msg.conflict: There is already an open RPL request for this
msg.narrative: Describe your experience in English (20-800 characters); Arabic is optional (20-800)
msg.state: This request is not in a state that allows that action
msg.self: Nobody decides their own RPL request
msg.maker_checker: The assessor who recommended this cannot confirm or return it: a second assessor is needed
msg.outcome: Choose full, partial or not-yet credit
msg.level_decide: Full credit is at the requested level; partial credit is a lower level; not-yet credits no level
msg.hours: Give the recognised notional hours as a whole number (1-600; 0 for not yet)
msg.rationale: Write the rationale in English and Arabic (20-800 characters each)
msg.not_attester: Only the named supervisor can answer this attestation
msg.text: Write the attestation in English (20-600 characters; Arabic optional) or a decline note of 10-400 characters
msg.not_signed_in: Sign in to work on recognition of prior learning
msg.forbidden_assessor: Only RPL assessors (instructors, the training manager and the HR director) recommend or confirm credit
msg.forbidden_export: Only the person and RPL assessors or auditors can export an RPL pack
msg.owner: Only the person who opened the request can change it
msg.limit: An evidence pack holds at most 12 items
msg.kind: Choose an evidence type from the list
msg.item: That record is not one of your attachable records
msg.security_restricted: Security-restricted records cannot be attached to an RPL pack
msg.duplicate: That item is already in the pack
msg.attester: Choose an active member of staff other than yourself (and other than the assessor who opened the request)
msg.too_few: Attach at least 2 evidence items before submitting
msg.records: Attach at least one record (practice, simulator, qualification or engagement), not only attestations

tagmsg.kind: Choose a course, a pathway or a micro-credential
tagmsg.not_live: Only courses, published pathways and current micro-credentials are tagged
tagmsg.not_found: There is no published tag to retire
tagmsg.nqf: Choose an indicative NQF level from 1 to 10
tagmsg.hours: Give the notional hours as a whole number from 1 to 1200 (1 credit = 10 hours)
tagmsg.basis: Explain the estimate in English and Arabic (20-300 characters each)
tagmsg.not_signed_in: Sign in to work with learning credits
tagmsg.forbidden: Only framework owners (instructors, the training manager and admins) tag learning with NQF levels and credits
tagmsg.forbidden_sync: You can refresh your own credit ledger; framework owners and assessors refresh anyone's

my.intro: Years of Barakah practice, simulator time and supervised work can count. Ask for credit on a skill or a micro-credential and build your evidence pack.
my.tOpenSub: Draft, submitted or awaiting the second assessor
my.tAttestSub: Colleagues asked you to confirm their practice
my.listDesc: Every request is kept, including withdrawn ones.
my.emptyBody: Start with a skill you practise every day.
my.creditsBody: Recognised hours join your credit ledger next to completed courses, pathways and micro-credentials.

start.title: Start an RPL request
start.body: Choose what you want recognised and say in your own words what you do. You will attach evidence next.
start.okBody: The request passes the same checks the server runs.

att.empty: Nobody has asked you to attest
att.emptyBody: When a colleague names you as their supervisor, the request appears here.
att.for: {name} asks you to confirm their practice for: {target}
att.confirmBody: Describe what you observed, when and how often. Do not include security detail.
att.declineBody: Say briefly why you cannot attest; the person sees your note.

queue.intro: Every decision needs two different assessors, and nobody decides their own request.
queue.tRecommendSub: Submitted packs awaiting a first assessor
queue.mcBody: The first assessor recommends full, partial or not-yet credit with a rationale; a second assessor confirms or returns it. The decision writes validated evidence and a ledger entry.
queue.behalf: Open a request for a contractor

behalf.title: Open a request for a contractor
behalf.body: Contractors have no Kafa'a grant: you open and assemble the pack from their mirrored engagements; they can read their request.
behalf.ok: You can open this request; another assessor must confirm any decision.

cr.intro: Every completed course, pathway and micro-credential that carries a tag, and every RPL credit, adds to your ledger. One credit is ten notional learning hours.
cr.how: How NQF levels and credits work
cr.syncUnknown: Some sources are not readable here
cr.syncNote: The ledger is rebuilt from completed items; rows that no longer count are marked reversed, never deleted.
cr.stacksDesc: Shown toward an indicative award with a partner university still to be agreed; RPL counts up to each stack's cap.

why.items: {n} counted items at NQF level {min} or above
why.rplCap: RPL credit capped at {max} (the stack's limit)

cr.ledgerDesc: One row per completed, tagged item. Reversed rows stay visible.

tags.intro: Every tag is an indicative NQF level and a credit value (1 credit = 10 notional hours). Every current micro-credential must carry one.
tags.mcOkBody: {n} of {n} carry an indicative NQF level and credits.
tags.listDesc: Courses, published pathways and current micro-credentials.
tags.retireBody: The tag is kept as retired and the ledger rows that used it are reversed at once.
tags.basisEn: How the level and hours were estimated (English)
tags.basisAr: How the level and hours were estimated (Arabic)
tags.checkOkBody: The tag passes the same checks the server runs.

pub.intro: Experienced staff and contractors can turn what they already do into recognised credit: an evidence pack from their own records, two assessors, and an indicative NQF level and credits.
pub.flowDesc: The ILO pattern: request, evidence, assessor, credit.

stepBody.request: Choose a skill at a level, or a micro-credential, and describe your experience.
stepBody.evidence: Attach your own records and ask a supervisor to attest.
stepBody.assess: One recommends full, partial or not-yet credit; a different one confirms.
stepBody.credit: Validated evidence updates your skills; hours join your credit ledger.

pub.evDesc: Only records already in Kafa'a, plus attestations the named supervisor confirms.

kindBody.ojt: OJT entries your preceptor acknowledged (walkthrough, simulated or performed).
kindBody.simulator: Crew simulator sessions with an instructor debrief.
kindBody.qualification: The qualification mirror, shown only as qualified or not qualified.
kindBody.engagement: Signed-off gigs, rotations and, for contractors, mirrored engagements.
kindBody.attestation: A supervisor's own words, confirmed by them in Kafa'a.

pub.neverBody: Security, safeguards and cyber records: they follow the security career path and are refused if attached.

outBody.full: Credit at the requested level, written as validated evidence.
outBody.partial: Credit at a lower level, with the rationale naming the gap.
outBody.not_yet: No credit yet; the rationale says what to add before trying again.

pub.twoPeople: A decision always needs two different assessors, and nobody decides their own request.
pub.export: A decided request exports as a pack that NQC-recognised assessors can review (initials only, roles not names).
pub.ctaSigned: Open your recognition page to start a request or see your credits.
pub.ctaAnon: Sign in with your role card to start a request.
pub.ruleBody: Notional hours include study and practice, not only contact time. Pathways count their practice and project component; courses inside them count separately.
pub.mapTitle: Kafa'a levels and the UAE NQF
pub.mapNote: NQF levels describe qualifications, not job proficiency; the map is loose and indicative.
pub.nqfSource: UAE Cabinet Resolution on the NQF
pub.stacksDesc: Thirty credits per stack; no partner university is named and no award is promised.
pub.catDesc: Every published tag, with how its level and hours were estimated.
pub.balTitle: A learning balance with protected study time
pub.balDesc: Staff get an annual learning balance they spend as protected study hours on an outcome-gated catalogue. Simulated in this demo.
pub.balGrantBody: {c} credits ({h} hours) a year, plus a {tc}-credit mid-career top-up from {y} years of service. Age is never used.
pub.balSpendBody: Only items of the outcome-gated catalogue: published, with published criteria every item meets.
pub.balTimeBody: Study hours are asked for in the portal and approved by the line manager (or the HR authority), never by the person.
pub.certDesc: Certificates from outside ENEC enter the record only after a verifier checks them with the issuer.
pub.certMap: A verified certificate maps to skills only through crosswalk rows that a second framework owner has reviewed; everything else stays "claimed".

sb.intro: Your learning entitlement for the year, shown as credits and hours (1 credit = 10 hours). Spend it as protected study time on items of the outcome-gated catalogue; your line manager approves each request. The figures are simulated.
sb.noBalanceBody: The learning balance and protected study time are for ENEC staff.
sb.balanceDesc: Grants minus approved use. Requests waiting for a decision are reserved.
sb.tAvailableSub: {h} hours ({r} hours left after approved use)

why.notEligible: Contractors and leavers have no learning balance.
why.base: Every member of staff gets {c} credits ({h} hours) a year.
why.topup: Mid-career top-up: {c} credits, because you had {y} years of service on 1 January (from {min}).
why.noTopup: No mid-career top-up yet: {y} years of service on 1 January (it starts at {min}).
why.neverAge: Years of service come from your HR record; age, gender and nationality are never used.
why.gated: In the outcome-gated catalogue: published and meeting every published criterion.
why.ungated: Not in the outcome-gated catalogue, so it cannot be charged to the balance.

sb.earned: You earned {c} credits from {n} completed items this year (FS30 ledger).
sb.howBody: Choose an item of the outcome-gated catalogue, ask for the study hours you need and say how they are protected (release days, blocks inside the roster or a week away from shift). The hours are reserved at once; your line manager approves or declines, never you. Only approved hours count as used.
sb.catDesc: Only items that are published and meet every published criterion can be charged to the balance.
sb.maxAsk: Up to {h} hours in one request
sb.alreadyOpen: You have an open request for this item
sb.reqDesc: Every request and decision is audited; approvals are also recorded in the NEXUS evidence ledger.
sb.withdrawBody: The hours go back to your balance. The request stays in your history.
sb.askBody: You can ask for up to {a} credits ({h} hours) this year.
sb.fReason: What the study time is for
sb.okBody: The hours will be reserved and your line manager will be told.
sb.confirmBody: {h} hours ({c} credits) will be reserved from your balance until your line manager decides.
sb.sent: Study time sent to your line manager
sb.simBody: Grants, top-ups and hours are simulated for this demo. No payroll, roster or HR system is connected, and nothing here changes a contract or a leave balance.
sb.teamIntro: Approve or decline protected study time for the people you manage. You never decide your own request.
sb.mcBody: The person asks; their line manager (or the HR authority when the line manager cannot) decides. Every decision is audited, and approvals write a NEXUS ledger row.
sb.queueEmpty: Nothing is waiting for a decision
sb.teamBalDesc: Balances of the people in your scope (simulated).
sb.approveBody: {name} gets {h} protected hours ({c} credits), charged to their balance. This writes an audit row and a NEXUS ledger row.
sb.declineBody: {name} keeps the hours in their balance. Say why, so they can send it again.
sb.hrIntro: How the simulated learning balances are granted and used. Any group of fewer than 10 people is suppressed.
sb.ruleBaseV: {c} credits ({h} hours) a year for every member of staff
sb.ruleTopupV: {c} more credits from {y} years of service on 1 January
sb.ruleSpend: What it can be spent on
sb.ruleSpendV: Only items of the outcome-gated catalogue (published, meeting every published criterion)
sb.ruleDecideV: The line manager in scope; the HR authority when the line manager cannot; never the person
sb.ruleNever: Age, gender and nationality are never inputs to the grant.
sb.useDesc: Groups of fewer than {n} people are suppressed.
sb.allSuppressed: Every group is under the minimum size
sb.hrDecideTitle: You can decide when the line manager cannot
sb.hrDecideBody: As the HR authority you can approve or decline a waiting request. You never decide your own.
sb.readOnlyBody: Only line managers and the HR authority decide study time.

xc.intro: Bring certificates from universities, professional bodies, vendors and online courses into your record. Each one reads as "claimed" until a verifier checks it with the issuer; then its trust tier shows wherever it appears, and only reviewed crosswalk rows turn it into skill evidence.
xc.tVerifiedSub: Checked with the issuer by a verifier
xc.tiersDesc: The tier is shown wherever the certificate appears: here, in the wallet, the learner record and on credential pages.

tierHelp.enec_assessed: Issued by ENEC and verified through an ENEC assessment.
tierHelp.accredited: A university or professional body with an accreditation reference, verified with the issuer.
tierHelp.vendor_self_serve: A vendor or online platform (or an issuer without an accreditation reference), verified with the issuer.
tierHelp.claimed: Not verified yet, or rejected or revoked. It never counts as evidence.

xc.emptyBody: Add one with the issuer's verification link.
xc.willMapAt: would map at level {l} once verified
xc.revokedNote: The verification was revoked: its evidence no longer counts.
xc.withdrawBody: It will no longer wait for verification. It stays in your history.
xc.addBody: Give the certificate details and the issuer's https verification link, then name the crosswalk entries it covers. A verifier checks it with the issuer.
xc.fAccHint: Leave empty if the issuer has none: the certificate is then vendor self-serve.
xc.fUrlHint: The issuer's page or registry entry for this certificate.
xc.previewNote: Levels are capped by the trust tier; entries that are not reviewed never map.
xc.okBody: It will read as "claimed" until a verifier checks it.
xc.confirmBody: A verifier will check it with the issuer. Nothing counts as evidence before that.
xc.sent: Certificate added: a verifier will check it

why.noAccreditation: It carries no accreditation reference, so it counts as vendor self-serve.

claimed.enec_assessed: Not verified yet: shown as claimed (it would be ENEC-assessed once verified).
claimed.accredited: Not verified yet: shown as claimed (it would be an accredited third party once verified).
claimed.vendor_self_serve: Not verified yet: shown as claimed (it would be vendor self-serve once verified).

verified.issuer_url: Verified on {date} through the issuer's verification link.
verified.issuer_registry: Verified on {date} in the issuer's registry.
verified.enec_assessment: Verified on {date} through an ENEC assessment.
verified.document_check: Verified on {date} by a document check.

why.cap: Skill evidence goes up to level {l} for this tier.
why.noEvidence: No skill evidence while it is not verified.

xc.qIntro: Check each certificate with its issuer, then verify, reject with a reason, or later revoke it. You never verify your own. Only reviewed crosswalk rows map to skills.
xc.tUnreviewedSub: Named but not reviewed: they will not map
xc.mcBody: A verifier who is not the holder decides. ENEC certificates are verified through an ENEC assessment; others through the issuer's link, registry or documents. Every decision is audited; verifying and revoking also write a NEXUS ledger row.
xc.readOnlyBody: Auditors read verifications; only verifiers decide.
xc.verifyBody: Its trust tier will show wherever it appears, and its reviewed crosswalk rows become skill evidence (levels capped by the tier). This writes an audit row and a NEXUS ledger row.
xc.rejectBody: It stays "claimed" and writes no evidence. Say why, so the holder can fix it.
xc.revokeBody: Its evidence becomes inactive and it reads "claimed" again. This writes an audit row and a NEXUS ledger row.

sbmsg.not_signed_in: Sign in to use your learning balance
sbmsg.forbidden_request: Only staff with a learning balance ask for protected study time
sbmsg.not_eligible: Protected study time and the learning balance are for ENEC staff (contractors and leavers have none)
sbmsg.item: Choose an item from the outcome-gated catalogue
sbmsg.ungated: Only items of the outcome-gated catalogue (published, meeting every published criterion) can be charged to the balance
sbmsg.hours: Ask for 2 to 40 whole hours, and no more than the item's notional hours
sbmsg.pattern: Choose how the study time is protected (release days, blocks inside the roster or a week away from shift)
sbmsg.dates: Give a start date from today and an end date in the same year, at most 92 days later
sbmsg.reason: Say in 10 to 300 characters what the study time is for
sbmsg.conflict: You already have an open request for this item this year
sbmsg.balance: Not enough learning balance left this year for these hours (pending requests are reserved)
sbmsg.no_line_manager: No line manager is recorded for you; ask HR to update your record
sbmsg.self: You cannot decide your own protected study time
sbmsg.forbidden: Only the line manager (or the HR authority) decides protected study time
sbmsg.state: This request is not waiting for a decision
sbmsg.note: Give a reason of at least 5 characters when you decline
sbmsg.late: This request has already ended; ask the person to send a new one
sbmsg.overdraw: Approving these hours would take the balance below zero
sbmsg.w_forbidden: Only the person who asked can withdraw a request
sbmsg.w_state: This request can no longer be withdrawn
sbmsg.w_started: The study time has already started; ask your line manager to close it
sbmsg.read_forbidden: You can read your own balance; line managers read their team's and HR reads everyone's

xcmsg.not_signed_in: Sign in to add an external certificate
xcmsg.forbidden_submit: You add and withdraw only your own certificates
xcmsg.forbidden_verify: Only verifiers (assessors and the HR authority) verify external certificates
xcmsg.title: Give the certificate title (3 to 160 characters)
xcmsg.issuer_kind: Choose the kind of issuer: ENEC, a university, a professional body, a vendor or an online platform
xcmsg.accreditation: The accreditation reference is at most 80 characters
xcmsg.credential_ref: Give the certificate or credential number (1 to 80 characters)
xcmsg.dates: Give an issue date up to today and, if it expires, an expiry date after it
xcmsg.url: Give an https verification link from the issuer (at most 300 characters)
xcmsg.alignments: Name 1 to 6 different crosswalk entries the certificate covers (published or under review, not retired)
xcmsg.levels: Claimed levels are whole numbers from 1 to 3 for the entries you named
xcmsg.note: The note is at most 300 characters
xcmsg.security_restricted: Security-area skills are recorded as qualified or not qualified only, never from external certificates
xcmsg.conflict: This certificate (same verification link) is already in your record
xcmsg.self: You cannot verify your own certificate
xcmsg.state: This certificate is not in a state for that decision
xcmsg.method: Choose how it was verified: issuer link, issuer registry, ENEC assessment or document check
xcmsg.method_tier: An ENEC-issued certificate is verified through an ENEC assessment, and only ENEC certificates are
xcmsg.expired: An expired certificate cannot be verified
xcmsg.reason: Give a reason of at least 5 characters
xcmsg.w_forbidden: Only the holder withdraws a certificate
xcmsg.w_state: Only a certificate waiting for verification can be withdrawn
